transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Evan Kim, Rosa Martinez, Priya Nair, Alex Grant, engineering/product org and others

[00:00] Jordan: Morning, everyone, thanks for joining, we're a little over an hour today, couple big updates, high level on Q1, then product, then people, then Q&A.
[00:25] Priya: Quick note, folks on timezones, recorded and slides up in the all-hands channel, feel free to drop questions there.
[00:35] Jordan: Kicking off with numbers. We closed the quarter with 48% quarter-over-quarter growth in hosted API usage, and a few big Dedicated deals came in last month that put bookings up — not sharing specifics here but it's healthy. Usage across embeddings also up, which is consistent with the PLG motion.
[01:10] Jordan: Latency p50 for small gen models is at 120ms on average, we've got pockets to improve, and cost per token is down ~12% after the batching and cache tweaks.
[01:30] Evan: Quick clarification — that 12% includes a mix of quantized runs and the new kernel selection in the runtime; there's some noise because some benchmarks hit different sequence lengths, but overall good signal.
[01:55] Jordan: On reliability, we had the March 11th incident, Evan can walk through the postmortem later. The net is we got better on sidecar restarts but we need more graceful KV cache warmups.
[02:15] Evan: Yeah, so — to be clear — the main issue was the prefix cache eviction pattern under a spike, our autoscaler overshot and the cold-start hit a path that wasn't rehydrating KV cache quickly. We patched a mitigation, but long term we need changes to the warmup flow and the scheduler heuristics. I'm leading the follow-up; will share the postmortem doc next week.
[02:45] Rosa: Product roadmap, high level — three themes for next 6 months: 1) Runtime performance (attention kernels, batching), 2) Private/enterprise features (VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM audit), and 3) Developer experience/Optimize (cost tooling, quantization suggestions).
[03:10] Rosa: We're pushing a Dedicated enhancement in April that gives better burst capacity and a deterministic SLA for p99 latency on common model families. It's a canary rollout with select customers.
[03:33] Alex: Sales note — please make sure the Dedicated SLA language and expected p99 numbers are in the deck, customers ask that up front. Also, we'll need any benchmark spreadsheets to attach.
[03:48] Rosa: Yep, will send the deck after this.
[03:55] Jordan: A quick customer highlight: one fintech customer moved to Dedicated and shaved 30% off inference cost per call while keeping latency under their 200ms target. Great example for sales.
[04:20] Alex: I'll put together a short case study for that — thanks.
[04:35] Priya: People updates — we're hiring across infra and product; interview loops are up, need help from ICs for panel availability. Also, leadership changes: welcoming Maya to Security as Head of Security, and Leah joining as Director of Sales Operations.
[05:00] Priya: Compensation review is in progress, we'll share timeline soon, not today though.
[05:12] Engineer (Speaker 1): Quick ops Q — are we planning any global region adds? APAC?
[05:20] Jordan: Yes, timeline for APAC region is H2, aiming to onboard a partner early for data center presence; more details after we complete the Private deployment checklist.
[05:40] Evan: Technical deep-dive coming next week on the kernel selection logic, that'll be SE-led, folks on infra and model ops should join.
[05:58] Rosa: On Redwood Optimize, we'll ship quantization profile suggestions for common workloads — basically a guided path to single-digit latency improvements without big quality loss.
[06:20] Rosa: Also we're adding a reranking tool to the console to help customers tune recall vs latency tradeoffs.
[06:40] Jordan: Security/compliance — Maya, can you share a quick update?
[06:45] Maya (Security): Sure. SOC2 readiness is on track; evidence collection is mostly automated now, a few manual artifacts remain. KMS integration is in internal beta with two customers, and we've got audit logging hooks in the private control plane. We'll publish the checklist to legal and sales by next week.
[07:10] Jordan: Great. On reliability, Evan, what are the immediate actions?
[07:18] Evan: Short term: tighten autoscaler thresholds, flip on staggered KV cache rehydration, and add better tracing for warmup. Mid-term: rework scheduler heuristics and improve kernel fallback fallthrough when sequence lengths spike.
[07:40] Speaker 2 (Product): Any update on model catalog curation? There's noise on OC models and metrics.
[07:48] Rosa: We're introducing an explicit verification profile — Redwood-verified performance tags — and a model catalog page in the console with per-model p50/p95, expected cost guidance. Will roll out in May.
[08:10] Jordan: On GTM, we're double downing on product-led content: benchmark stories, how-to guides for Dedicated, and reference infra templates. Also exploring cloud marketplace integrations.
[08:30] Alex: Partnerships update — in preliminary talks with a regional cloud partner in APAC and one reseller for regulated customers. Nothing committed yet.
[08:45] Jordan: Questions from the room?
[08:50] Speaker 3 (Eng): For the canary Dedicated rollout, will it require code changes from customers?
[08:58] Rosa: No, primarily config-level. Some customers on self-hosted private may want small networking tweaks, but hosted Dedicated shouldn't require app changes.
[09:15] Speaker 4 (Sales): Pricing question: will Dedicated bursts cost more on top of reserved capacity?
[09:25] Alex: Yes there will be a burst premium; details in the pricing doc, we'll send a note to sales.
[09:40] Jordan: Quick recap — roadmap deck, ops postmortem, hiring priorities, security checklist, and sales case studies. Action owners assigned in the next steps channel.
[09:55] Priya: We'll run smaller team-specific all-hands to follow up on execution plans.
[10:05] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll publish recording and materials; drop follow-ups in the all-hands channel.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., K-V cache sometimes shows up as k-v cash, VPC as V-P-C) and filler words remain; this is a verbatim-ish capture, not cleaned up.
